rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4-5 (Model development/simulation; Simulation results) report the authors' own Proteus simulation runs of a Raspberry Pi/MCP3208 sensor framework with simulated temperature, pressure, soil moisture and rain inputs over a 1-hour period, plus a mobile app displaying the simulated data.
rows.notes: The study is a design-and-simulation paper, not a field trial. It simulates sensor readings using predefined input ranges (temperature 20-40 C, soil moisture 10-50%, etc.) in Proteus and shows that data flow to ThingSpeak and app alerts work. No crop was grown, no yield, water use or environmental impact was measured, and the simulation output was never compared with measurements from a real system (Sections 5.5 and 6 state it used predefined data and no real-world devices). Claims about improved yields, optimized irrigation and reduced waste appear only as assertions or citations ([18], [19]). At most the study demonstrates a monitoring/alerting capability that is a precondition of the claimed yield benefit, so it is upstream of the claim. The limitation statements (predefined data, no calibration, experimental setup) refer to the simulation itself, not to any result on crop production, so Q8 is 'no' following the Q2 rule.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study contains no empirical agronomic results; it is a Proteus simulation of an IoT weather/soil monitoring framework with a mobile app, intended for Ugandan farmers but not deployed.
